messages:

Subject: Clarify token accounting, context floors, and pilot discounts

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Nimble liked the latency profile and the KV-cache reuse idea. Before we move to a pilot, finance asked for clear language on three items so we can sign off:

1) How tokens are accounted for streaming + long-context use cases (our agents stream user input live, then append a ~6k token conversation history). Do you bill streaming tokens differently?
2) Minimums / rounding: we have many short interactions (~30–80 tokens each) interspersed with long sessions. How does Redwood handle the minimum billing quantum and rounding across these mixed patterns?
3) Discounts for pilot: we discussed a promotional rate — can you confirm a pilot discount and whether it applies to both hosted and dedicated capacity?

If you can send a one-page worked example with numbers for our CFO and an invoice sample, that would speed approvals.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Product
Nimble Retail

P.S. Attached is our expected traffic profile (lightly redacted) — happy to walk through it live.

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@nimbleretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify token accounting, context floors, and pilot discounts

Hi Samir — great to hear Nimble found the demo useful. Short answers up front, then a proposed MA/plan: 

- Streaming tokens: billed the same as non-streamed tokens (we meter produced + consumed tokens). We do not currently have a separate streaming surcharge.
- Minimums & rounding: default quantum is 1,024 token units per request for hosted plans; however we offer session-level rollups where consecutive calls within a 5 minute interactive window aggregate toward the quantum. We also provide a per-conversation amortization option for long history sessions to reduce impact of many small bursts.
- Pilot discount: we can offer a pilot discount (details below) that applies to hosted API only by default; dedicated can be included with a committed capacity addendum.

Attached: "Nimble_Retail_pricing_sample_v2.xlsx" with three worked examples (short bursts, mixed, long-chat). Key takeaways (from the sheet):

• Example A — high frequency short bursts (avg request 60 tokens, 20k calls/month): effective rounding cost adds ~5% without amortization; with session rollup it drops to ~1.2%.
• Example B — mixed (avg 800 tokens, occasional 6k context): session amortization yields 40–60% savings on context reuse when KV cache hit rate > 30%.
• Example C — streaming long sessions: identical billing model, but we recommend a model variant with longer sequence optimization (reduces token compute by ~12%).

Proposed mutual action plan:
1) Quick sync (30m) to confirm concurrency / average context length so we pick correct amortization policy.
2) Pilot (3 months) on Hosted API with tracking: apply pilot discount to tokens and embeddings.
3) After pilot, decide whether to move to Dedicated with committed GPU hours.

Can Kimberly (cc'd) confirm discount flexibility and whether we can extend to dedicated with a commit?

Cheers,
Chloe Martin

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify token accounting, context floors, and pilot discounts

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask and thanks Chloe for the worked examples. A couple of concrete items from the commercial side: 

1) Pilot discount: we can offer a 15% discount on token and embedding spend for the first 3 months, applied to Hosted API charges. If Nimble commits to a 12-month post-pilot Dedicated reservation at >= $50k/mo equivalent, we will extend the 15% to the Dedicated line and an additional 5% committed discount (so 20% total during the committed term).

2) Rounding & minimums: we will honor session amortization for the pilot. Operationally this means: token consumption is bucketized into 1,024-token quanta per request but aggregated per-session over 5 minute interactive windows. Any remaining partial quantum at invoice time is rounded up to the nearest quantum unless amortization is enabled, in which case leftover partials from the same session are merged. Example: 12 calls of 60 tokens each => 720 tokens total. Without amortization that's billed as 12 * 1,024 quanta; with amortization that's billed as 1 quantum (1,024) plus 0 partials charged pro-rata. See the attached spreadsheet for numerical walk-through.

3) KV/prefix reuse credit: as a commercial concession for pilots, if measured KV reuse (across your workload) is > 30% we will apply a one-time credit equal to the estimated CPU/GPU savings (calculated from the telemetry) capped at 10% of that month’s token charges. This is intended to align incentives and reduce initial friction.

4) Streaming: streaming tokens are counted identical to non-streamed tokens. However, for high-throughput streaming patterns we can route you to a long-sequence optimized variant which often reduces billed token compute by ~10–15% on our end — we'll show the delta in the pilot analytics.

Next steps:
• Chloe — please schedule a 30m call this week to confirm concurrency and to send an invoice sample for the pilot (finance requested one).
• Samir — if you sign off on the 15% pilot discount and the KV reuse credit terms, we'll prepare a one-page pilot addendum and DocuSign link.

Kimberly Park
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Thanks Chloe and Kimberly — this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side before we sign the pilot addendum: 

• Confirmed: the 15% pilot discount applies to tokens + embeddings on Hosted. If we move to Dedicated with a 12-month commit, we'll get the extra 5% (20% total) — please include this in the DocuSign addendum.

• Invoice sample: finance asked for a sample invoice showing a mixed-month (20k small bursts, 1,500 long sessions with avg 5k context). Can you generate that sample and include the KV reuse credit line (if applicable)?

• Streaming nuance: we stream user keystrokes into an endpoint and frequently append partial tokens to the conversation. If you count consumed + produced tokens together, how are partial tokens aggregated? For example, if an event stream sends 6 partial frames that total 90 tokens, does Redwood aggregate those into one quantum or treat them as 6 separate small requests?

If you can send the doc for signature with the invoice sample attached, we can get finance to review and move to pilot next week.

Appreciate it —
Samir
